solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Outside pub indifferent setter’s uttering oaths (9)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is a gerund phrase; BLASPHEMY is the noun for the act.

indicatorNotes.Outside: BLASE sits outside PH, wrapping it

annotation.surface: A blasé crossword setter stands outside the pub swearing.
annotation.walkthrough: PH is the map abbreviation for a public house. The setter referring to themself gives ME or MY.
annotation.definitionFit: Blasphemy is irreverent talk about God, the sort of oath-swearing the phrase describes.

entries.clue: Claret-stained bachelor cashed in chips after game (8)

blocks.note: loo is an old card game
to cash in one's chips = to die

indicatorNotes.after: one thing coming after another in time puts the dying at the end, behind the game

annotation.surface: A bachelor at the card table finishes the evening with wine on his shirt.
annotation.walkthrough: Claret is old boxing slang for blood, so 'claret-stained' is not about wine. Loo is an old card game, not only a lavatory.
annotation.definitionFit: Claret is slang for blood, so claret-stained means bloodied.

entries.clue: American cartel ultimately behind recording (5)

annotation.surface: An American cartel appears to be the power behind some recording.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a position word but is the noun: a bum.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an LP or CD of collected tracks is a recording released as one.

entries.clue: Praise God for one song missing line (9)

annotation.surface: A hymn praising God has lost a line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Praise God' reads as a hymn's opening; 'Praise' is the definition and 'God' starts the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A panegyric is a speech or text of high praise.

entries.clue: Land English scoundrel in trouble? On the contrary! (7)

indicatorNotes.On the contrary!: swap the roles: the trouble goes in the scoundrel, not the other way round

annotation.surface: An English scoundrel lands himself in trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: Read literally, the English scoundrel would sit inside the trouble; 'On the contrary!' flips it so the trouble sits inside the scoundrel.
annotation.definitionFit: Ecuador is a country, a land in South America.

entries.clue: Undergarment father wearing that way up (1-6)

indicatorNotes.wearing: YON wears FR, holding it inside
indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, 'up' turns ST round to TS

blocks.note: yon = that, as in yon hill

annotation.surface: Father puts on his underwear the right way up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'That way up' reads as one phrase about orientation; it splits into YON (that) and ST (way) with 'up' turning only the way. Y-fronts are men's briefs with a Y-shaped front seam.
annotation.definitionFit: Y-fronts are a style of men's underpants.

entries.clue: Black eye for malevolent sprite (5)

blocks.note: to ogle is to eye up

annotation.surface: A black eye is the work of some malicious imp.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Black eye' reads as a bruise, but eye is the verb, to ogle. A bogle is a goblin in Scottish and northern folklore.
annotation.definitionFit: A bogle is a goblin or bogey, a mischievous or evil spirit.

entries.clue: Boring thing to hold iron over suit (5)

indicatorNotes.to hold: BIT holds the iron inside it
indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, FE turned over reads EF

blocks.note: FE, the symbol for iron, turned over

annotation.surface: A dull chore: ironing a suit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boring' means dull on the surface but drilling in the wordplay: a bit is the boring tool.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: what suits the occasion is fitting for it, as in 'clothes that befit a funeral'.

entries.clue: Biscuit from German in hotel filling belly (6,3)

indicatorNotes.in: a guest staying in a hotel is inside it, so GER is placed inside INN
indicatorNotes.filling: a filling sits inside a sandwich or pie, so these letters go inside GUT

annotation.surface: A German in a hotel fills his belly with biscuits.
annotation.walkthrough: The assembly nests twice: GER into INN, then INGERN into GUT. A ginger nut is a hard ginger-flavoured biscuit, a British favourite for dunking in tea.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the ginger nut is one particular kind of biscuit, named for its ginger flavour and hard, nutty snap.

entries.clue: Most senior earl with lord is in Versailles (6)

annotation.surface: At the court of Versailles, the most senior noble is an earl alongside a lord.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In Versailles' asks for the French word: 'is' is EST.
annotation.definitionFit: Seniority here is by age: the first-born of a family, the oldest sibling, outranks the rest.

entries.clue: Soldiers refuse to allow leader in Europe (5)

blocks.note: to ban = to refuse to allow

annotation.surface: Troops refuse to let a European leader through.
annotation.walkthrough: Viktor Orbán was the long-serving prime minister of Hungary. OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword soldiers.
annotation.definitionFit: Viktor Orbán led Hungary's government, a leader in Europe.

entries.clue: Unchecked imports initially fresh and raw (9)

annotation.surface: Unregulated imports arrive fresh and raw.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Imports' reads as trade goods but is the verb: UNREINED takes the F in.
annotation.definitionFit: Unrefined means in a raw, unprocessed state.

entries.clue: Dido involved with male — eg Aeneas? (7)

annotation.definitionNote: The question mark shows Aeneas is one example of a demigod.

blocks.note: M = male, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: Queen Dido's love affair with the hero Aeneas.
annotation.walkthrough: In Virgil's Aeneid, Dido, queen of Carthage, falls for Aeneas, son of the goddess Venus and the mortal Anchises. 'eg' looks like a pointer to an example but is two letters of fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Aeneas, born of a goddess and a mortal, is a demigod.

entries.clue: Small stone cask around some trees (7)

indicatorNotes.around: to turn around is to face back the way you came, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: a gem is a precious stone
a tun is a large cask

annotation.surface: A small stone cask sits among a stand of trees.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like it wants a container, but here it turns the whole string back to front. A tun is a big brewer's cask.
annotation.definitionFit: Nutmegs are tropical evergreen trees that bear the spice, so some trees.

entries.clue: Unknown individual on a starship improving area (10,4)

blocks.note: the starship Enterprise of Star Trek

indicatorNotes.on: in an across answer, one piece written on another follows it, so the unknown individual comes after the starship

annotation.surface: A mysterious person aboard a starship improves the place.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' reads as 'aboard' in the surface. An enterprise zone is a UK area given tax breaks to encourage regeneration.
annotation.definitionFit: An enterprise zone is a designated area set up to improve its economy.

entries.clue: Engine right in clumsy boat round shore (9)

indicatorNotes.in: a passenger is in a boat, so the R sits inside TUB

blocks.note: a tub is a slow, clumsy boat

annotation.surface: An engine sits in a clumsy boat going round the shore.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shore' is the verb to shore up, a prop, not the coast.
annotation.definitionFit: A turboprop is a jet engine that drives a propeller.

entries.clue: Find ale brewed with New Zealand wine grape (9)

blocks.note: NZ = New Zealand, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: Hunting for some beer made with a New Zealand grape.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brewed' fits the ale so well that it hides its job as the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Zinfandel is a black wine grape, much grown in California.

entries.clue: Curved screen deployed in court (8)

indicatorNotes.in: the rearranged letters go inside CT

annotation.surface: A curved screen is set up in a courtroom.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Curved screen' reads as one object; 'Curved' is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: Crescent can be an adjective meaning curved like the new moon.

entries.clue: College official retains drunk artisan who delays jobs? (14)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is a relative clause standing for 'one who delays jobs'; the answer is that person.

indicatorNotes.retains: to retain is to hold on to, so PROCTOR holds the rest inside
indicatorNotes.drunk: a drunk staggers all over the place, so the letters of 'artisan' lurch out of order

blocks.note: a proctor keeps discipline at Oxford and Cambridge

annotation.surface: A university official keeps a drunken craftsman who never gets round to the work.
annotation.walkthrough: The artisan belongs to the wordplay, not the definition, though the surface fuses them.
annotation.definitionFit: A procrastinator is someone who keeps putting tasks off.

entries.clue: Pardon a second-rate answer? (7)

blocks.note: to answer a problem is to solve it

annotation.surface: Please excuse a mediocre reply.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pardon' reads as 'excuse me?' asking for a repeat; it is the verb to forgive. 'Answer' is a verb too.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: a priest who pardons sins absolves the penitent.

entries.clue: Meat in a mouse more than enough for bird (7)

indicatorNotes.more than enough for: the phrase holds more letters than the bird needs, and the bird sits within them

annotation.surface: The meat inside a mouse would feed a bird and then some.
annotation.walkthrough: The unusual indicator says the phrase is more than the bird needs, so the answer lies inside it. A tinamou is a ground bird of Central and South America.
annotation.definitionFit: The tinamou is a partridge-like South American bird.

entries.clue: Slogger’s run out; Jack Brown’s caught (6)

indicatorNotes.caught: TAN catches RO and J inside it

blocks.note: RO = run out on a cricket scorecard

annotation.surface: A cricket report: the big hitter is run out and Jack Brown caught.
annotation.walkthrough: The cricket surface hides the definition: a slogger here is a hard worker, someone who works like a Trojan, not a batsman who swings hard. 'Run out' is a way to lose a wicket.
annotation.definitionFit: To work like a Trojan is to slog away, so a Trojan is a slogger.

entries.clue: Ungovernable route northwest from Ipanema? (7)

blocks.note: Ipanema is a beach district of Rio de Janeiro
heading northwest from Brazil you go TO the US

annotation.surface: A travel question: which unruly road runs northwest out of Ipanema?
annotation.walkthrough: The route is spelled out as a journey: RIO TO US.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a mob that has broken into riot is beyond anyone's power to govern.

entries.clue: Old Cordelier’s end perhaps in French commune (5)

indicatorNotes.end: take the last letter of Cordelier
indicatorNotes.perhaps: 'say' is how you mark an example, so SAY = perhaps

annotation.surface: An old Franciscan friar meets his end in a French town.
annotation.walkthrough: Cordeliers were French Franciscan friars, and the name of a revolutionary club, which fits the French scene. Orsay is a town southwest of Paris.
annotation.definitionFit: Orsay is a commune in the Essonne department near Paris.

entries.clue: Subtle variations one’s not seen among pests (7)

indicatorNotes.not seen among: I'S is taken out from the middle of NUISANCES

annotation.surface: Subtle differences you can't see among the insects.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One's' gives I'S, with the apostrophe dropped as usual.
annotation.definitionFit: Nuances are subtle differences of meaning, tone or colour.

entries.clue: Activists in church guarding a medic (5)

indicatorNotes.guarding: a guard stands all round what it protects, so CE surrounds the rest

annotation.surface: Protesters in a church are protecting a doctor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' is the link here; 'guarding' does the containing.
annotation.definitionFit: A cadre is a core group of trained political activists.

entries.clue: Rule judge reversed protects Liberal in holy city (9)

indicatorNotes.reversed: turn MEASURE and J round together

blocks.note: a rule is a measure, a measuring stick

annotation.surface: A judge's ruling is overturned to protect a Liberal in the holy city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rule' is a noun: a ruler or measure, not a verdict.
annotation.definitionFit: Jerusalem is holy to Jews, Christians and Muslims.

entries.clue: Try to avoid vehicle involved in many collisions leaving motorway (5)

blocks.note: a dodgem is a bumper car
M = motorway, as in the M1

annotation.surface: Advice to steer clear of a car that keeps crashing as you leave the motorway.
annotation.walkthrough: Dodgems are fairground bumper cars built for collisions. British motorways are numbered M1, M25 and so on.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: you dodge a question or a blow by trying to avoid it, sidestepping.

entries.clue: Where baby goes to sleep, possibly exhausted (5)

indicatorNotes.exhausted: 'possibly' emptied of its middle, leaving P and Y

blocks.note: a nap is a short sleep

annotation.surface: A baby is put down to sleep, worn out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Where baby goes to sleep' pulls toward a cot; 'goes' means to relieve itself, and 'to' only links. A nappy is a diaper.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic-leaning description: 'go' is the nursery euphemism for relieving oneself, and a baby does that into a diaper.

entries.clue: Net at sea keeping cows mostly buoyant (9)

indicatorNotes.at sea: someone all at sea is confused and lost, so the letters of 'net' are jumbled
indicatorNotes.keeping: to keep something is to hold it, so ENT holds BULLIE inside
indicatorNotes.mostly: most but not all of the word, so BULLIES loses its last letter

blocks.note: BULLIES (cows, intimidates) minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A fishing net out at sea holds up some cattle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cows' is the verb, to intimidate or bully, not the farm animals.
annotation.definitionFit: Ebullient means cheerful and full of energy, buoyant.
